Fabrication of the Perovskite Hybrid Solar Cells (Pero-HSCs) : The
pero-HSCs were fabricated in the device with a conﬁ guration of ITO/
PEDOT:PSS/CH 3 NH 3 PbI 3- x Cl x /PC 61 BM/Al, where ITO is indium tin
oxide, CH 3 NH 3 PbI 3- x Cl x is perovskite materials, and Al is Aluminum.
Approximately 35 nm of PEDOT:PSS was spin-coated on precleaned ITO
glass substrates followed by thermal annealing at 150 °C for 10 min.
The perovskite ﬁ lms were spin-coated on top of ITO/PEDOT:PSS from
perovskite precursor solution in the glove box with nitrogen atmosphere.
The perovskite thin ﬁ lms were processed by two-step procedures.

All materials else were purchased from J&K Scientific
Ltd and used as received. Substrates of the cells are fluorine-
doped tin oxide conducting glass (FTO, Pilkington, thickness:
2.2mm, sheet resistance 14Ω/square). CH_{3}NH_{3}I was synthesized
as the literature ^{33}.
20

First, laser-patterned, FTO-coated glass substrates were
cleaned by ultrasonication in an alkaline, aqueous washing
solution, rinsed with deionized water, ethanol, acetone and 2-
propanol, respectively. A hole-blocking layer of compact TiO2
25
with a thickness of about 50nm was deposited by a dip-coating
method with a TiO2 organic solution 34-35, and then followed by a
sintering process at 500℃ for 30min. After cooling to room
temperature, the substrates were treated in an 40mM aqueous
solution of TiCl4 at 70℃ for 30min, rinsed with deionized water
30
and dried at 500℃ for 30min. The mesoporous TiO2 layer with a
thickness of 180nm was prepared as previously reported 17.

PSCs were fabricated on ﬂuorine-doped tin oxide (FTO)-coated
glass substrates (Pilkington, Tec-8), which were patterned us-
ing Zn powder and a dilute HCl solution, followed by cleaning
with diluted Hellmanex, acetone, ethanol, and deionized water.
Amorphous-SnO 2 was prepared as an ESL on the FTO glass by
spin coating 0.1 M tin(II) chloride dihydrate solution in ethanol
(Sigma-Aldrich) at 30 0 0 rpm for 30 s. After drying at 100 °C for
1 min, the sample was instantly transferred to an IPL apparatus
(HI-PULSE 15,0 0 0, PSTEK) for treatment using different ﬂash counts
delivering different amounts of energy. Fig.

of ITO/HTL/PTB7:PC_{71}BM/LiF/Al and perovskite solar cells
with a structure of ITO/HTL/CH_{3}NH_{3}PbI_{x}Cl_{3−x}/PC_{61}BM/Bphen/
Ag were fabricated to investigate the functions of the aqueous-
solution-processed MoO_{3}, GeO_{2}, V_{2}O_{5} and CrO_{3} HTLs. PEDOT:
PSS (Baytron PVP Al 4083) based devices were also fabricated
for comparison. After HTL deposition, the substrates were
transferred into a glovebox for active layer coating.

The only exception was the rapid reduction, where the champion cell had a 5.9% e ffi ciency ( Figure 3D). Topdown and cross-sectional SEM images recorded for samples post-treated with the rapid reduction revealed that the degradation of the MAPbI3 layers can be avoided using this strategy (Figure S8).

The electrochemical deposition of PEDOT o ff ers a convenient way to deposit a hole-transport layer on a MAPbI3 layer for designing n -i -p junction perovskite solar cells. By employing potentiostatically controlled electrodeposition technique, it is possible to obtain controlled thicknesses of HTM layers. An electrochemical postreduction step introduced to control the doping level of the as-deposited PEDOT fi lms is an essential step in achieving better performance of PSCs. Care should be exercised not to destroy the underlying MAPbI3 layer during the post-treatment process. The champion device showed a power conversion e ffi ciency of 5.9%.
